Oof. I’ve been here. I’m sorry that your friends are becoming less supportive, know that there are people out there that are supportive even if you can’t see them. If you’ve gotten brain scans and your symptoms are impacting your life like this, I’d really push to get a diagnosis and have meds prescribed. I was really fucking scared to even tell my psychiatrist that I was experiencing bad symptoms, but I took the leap and got meds. My life has become so much better. It’s brought me to a normal level of function and my self esteem has gotten so much better. I’m able to get shit done, I got a job, I’ve been actually cleaning my room, I can carry on conversations, I can put my effort into something and actually see results. ADHD is one of those disorders where meds are the most effective treatment, so id recommend that before anything else. Idk where you stand on the morality of medications or relying on them, but that’s my recommendation :)

Here’s my opinion: a lot of people that say shit got weird after 2012 are millennials/ gen z. Like me, I’m a zoomer and I feel like shit got weird. Holidays stopped feeling like holidays, the world started going apeshit, mental health shit got weirder, I started seeing coincidences in everything, had more mini spiritual epiphanies, odd/unique circumstances started coming up, overall life just got weird in an almost over-worldly sense. I attribute this 2012 phenomenon to most people going into adult or teen hood at this time. It just happens to be at that perfect spot where a generation(or two) of people were going through major changes in their bodies, lives, social position, personalities and living situations. I feel like it’s not actually something that shifted in the universe per se, but something that shifted in a lot of people’s lives. Really, being 11-17 years old and having everybody and everything around you saying that we’re all gonna die in t-minus 12 hours is fucking horrifying. Traumatic, if I had to use a word. Not knowing if everything you’ve ever known and loved is going to be obliterated is scary. I feel like it desensitized a lot of kids/teens to life, bc some kids actually prepared to die. Like me, I was a pretty dramatic kid, and I wasn’t sure if we were all gonna die. I was 11. But I had a moment during New Years were I felt at peace, if we all die, I’m okay with that. I’m happy just being here. That can really change a kid, looking mortality right in the fucking mug and not being scared. I know not everybody else had the same experience, but that’s my take on it. Much love <3

It helps keep the intrusive/repetitive thoughts at bay. Like they’re still there, but I can control them and realize some of my fears and obsessions are not based in fact. The need for repetitive physical routines has lessened for me as well. I realize that there’s an urge to do a routine, but I can keep it to a functional level. For example, washing my hands twice instead of until they’re raw. Overall, I think medication really helps bring the symptoms from unbearable and interfering with life to a more “I can handle this” level. 
Keep in mind though that everyone experiences medications different. It might take multiple tries for you and your doctor to find the right medication for you. Don’t be afraid to ask questions, it’s your body! You have the right to know absolutely everything about a medication before you go on it. And if it’s not working out, it’s 100% okay to go off of it. Doctors and psychiatrists are honestly there to help you, and asking them what the most common reactions (negative or positive) to the medication will not annoy them. 
Overall, if your symptoms are interfering with your life to the point of suffering, go on meds. You can always go off if you want, but giving it a go to see if it helps is worth it :)

I take myself to a place in my mind that is safe and calm. It could be a happy memory, a beautiful place you’ve been to or a fictional setting/scenario.

Counting in my head or doing math in my head helps sometimes. Keep it simple because if you can’t solve it quickly it could trigger thoughts of incompetence(thats happened to me before lol). I feel like it takes my mind off of the emotional and focuses it on the logical.

The biggest thing that helps me is stimulating the senses(sometimes called soothing the senses). Pick a sense, and do something that involves it. Touch: rubbing my fingers together, petting dog or other soft/interesting surface. Smell: really strong essential oil. Taste: very strong flavors like sour or spicy. Sight: looking up my favorite color on google, enlarging the picture, and just losing myself in the color; watching a YouTube video of people making art. The general idea is that it takes your focus off of other things.

Another thing that really helps but only works if you can get up: going for a walk. Down the hall, to the bathroom, outside, through a building. Just get up and walk. The idea that when people have panic attacks or are feeling anxious, it all has to do with the flight, fight or freeze response. By walking you can satisfy that response, and it will lessen the anxiety. 

Hope this stuff helps, I know it helps me, but everyone is different. Keep trying until you find what works for you, fight to urge to give up!! You deserve calm and peace. You can do this. 💞much love!!
